To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed regression modeling and estimation procedures for censored survival time data with delayed effects are consistent and asymptotically normal.
the methods developed in this dissertation can be used to analyze survival data with delayed effects, and that they can be applied to the analysis of data from a large-scale randomized trial.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the statistical modeling of survival data with lagged effects.
the analysis of survival data with lagged effects.
the analysis of survival data when the effect of some covariate may be delayed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methods provide a useful tool for the analysis of survival data with lagged effects.
the lag models proposed in this paper provide a useful and flexible framework for analyzing survival data subject to delayed effects of some covari- ables.
the methods described in this paper are applicable to a wide range of problems in the analysis of survival data, with and without censoring.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a new model for survival data that can handle right censored data with lagged effects, we provide the maximum likelihood estimation for the model parameters, and we apply the model to a real clinical trial.

the proposed methods can be useful for the design and analysis of randomized clinical trials with delayed treatment effects, and for the analysis of observational studies with delayed effects of exposure.
the lag effect model can be used to analyze survival data with delayed effects of covariates and that the model can be used for interim analyses of clinical trials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lagged effects are important to consider in survival analysis.
the inclusion of lag effects in regression models for survival data can lead to more realistic and more powerful analyses of the data, especially in the presence of censoring.
the inclusion of covariates that are delayed in effect can have a substantial impact on the interpretation of survival data.
